Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, reference density $\rho_*>0$ in kilograms per cubic metre, reference speed $U_*>0$ in metres per second, physical polytropic coefficient $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}>0$ in pascals times $(\mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{kg})^\gamma$, and dimensionless exponent $\gamma>1$. Let the physical periodic cell be $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi L\mathbb Z))^d$, with position $X$ in metres and time $t$ in seconds. The physical density $\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}$ is measured in kilograms per cubic metre, velocity $u_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in metres per second, and pressure $p_{\mathrm{phys}}$ in pascals. Adopt the unforced, positive-density barotropic Euler model
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}+\nabla_X\cdot(\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}u_{\mathrm{phys}})=0,\qquad \partial_tu_{\mathrm{phys}}+(u_{\mathrm{phys}}\cdot\nabla_X)u_{\mathrm{phys}}+\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^{-1}\nabla_X\!\left(\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^\gamma\right)=0,$$
where the same fixed $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}$ and $\gamma$ apply throughout the flow. Set $x=X/L\in\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z))^d$, $\tau=tU_*/L$, $R=\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}/\rho_*$, $V=u_{\mathrm{phys}}/U_*$, $P=p_{\mathrm{phys}}/(\rho_*U_*^2)$, and $\bar\kappa=\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_*^{\gamma-1}/U_*^2>0$. Put $a=(\gamma-1)/2$ and $r(R)=\sqrt{\bar\kappa\gamma}\,R^a/a$. For smooth periodic $f$, use normalized measure $d\mu_x=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, Fourier coefficients $\widehat f(k)=\int f(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu_x$, and $\|f\|_{H^m}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}(1+|k|^2)^m|\widehat f(k)|^2$. Let $\rho_0:\mathbb T_L^d\to(0,\infty)$ and $u_0:\mathbb T_L^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be smooth real periodic initial data, and define $R_0(x)=\rho_0(Lx)/\rho_*$ and $V_0(x)=u_0(Lx)/U_*$. Then for every integer $s\ge4$ there is $T>0$, depending only on $d,s,\bar\kappa,\gamma,\|(r(R_0),V_0)\|_{H^s}$, and $\min r(R_0)$, such that the normalized system
$$\partial_\tau R+\nabla_x\cdot(RV)=0,\qquad \partial_\tau V+(V\cdot\nabla_x)V+R^{-1}\nabla_x(\bar\kappa R^\gamma)=0,\qquad R(0,\cdot)=R_0,\quad V(0,\cdot)=V_0$$
has a unique smooth real solution on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ with $R(\tau,x)>0$ and every integer Sobolev order $m\ge s$ bounded on that same interval. The dimensionless mean total-energy density
$$\overline E(\tau)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\left(\tfrac12 R|V|^2+\frac{\bar\kappa}{\gamma-1}R^\gamma\right)d\mu_x$$
is constant. Equivalently, the physical mean of $\tfrac12\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}|u_{\mathrm{phys}}|^2+\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}^\gamma/(\gamma-1)$ over the physical cell is constant and has units of pascals. The polytropic pressure law is an adopted constitutive closure, not a molecular derivation. No thermal equation, vacuum, shock continuation, nonuniform-entropy model, or empirical validity claim is included.

derivations.claim: Since $\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}$ and $u_{\mathrm{phys}}$ are constant in $t$ and $X$, $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}=0$, $\nabla_X\cdot(\rho_{\mathrm{phys}}u_{\mathrm{phys}})=0$, and $\partial_tu_{\mathrm{phys}}+(u_{\mathrm{phys}}\cdot\nabla_X)u_{\mathrm{phys}}=0$. Thus the mass equation holds.

The pressure $\kappa_{\mathrm{phys}}\rho_*^\gamma$ is constant, so its gradient vanishes; the momentum equation also holds. The density stays strictly positive, and all fields are smooth and periodic.
